title: House committee advances bill to ban sheriffs’ agreements with ICE, a day after Senate panel OK
summary: The House Judiciary Committee pushed through a bill Wednesday to ban agreements between local police and federal immigration authorities, amending it to make it emergency legislation that would take effect immediately on signing by the governor.
content:
by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters January 28, 2026

by William J. Ford, Maryland Matters January 28, 2026

The House Judiciary Committee pushed through a bill Wednesday to ban agreements between local police and federal immigration authorities, amending it in the process to make it emergency legislation that would take effect immediately on signing by the governor.

The 12-7 committee vote on House Bill 444 came one day after the Senate Judicial Proceedings Committee approved its own version of the bill, Senate Bill 245. Each of the fast-tracked bills could be debated in their respective chambers as early as Thursday.

The Senate bill is not emergency legislation but the sponsor of the House bill, Del. Nicole Williams (D-Prince George’s), said she hopes the Senate will make that change.

“It’s exciting to have our support from our friends across the street. This bill is a long time coming,” Williams said, after the House committee’s roughly 35-minute voting session. “We’ll see if they do an amendment on the floor. We believe the emergency measure is imperative, just really kind of everything we’re seeing [and] going on across the country. This is a necessity.”

Both committee votes come as scrutiny grows over the aggressive immigration enforcement policies of the Trump administration, including the fatal shootings in Minneapolis this month of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, both 37, by federal immigration agents.

Senate panel advances bills to ban agreements with ICE, face coverings for law enforcement

House Majority Leader David Moon (D-Montgomery), who serves on the Judiciary Committee, said the Immigration and Customs Enforcement tactics generating headlines now are not new. Advocates and immigrant rights groups tried to pass a ban last year on 287(g) agreements. It passed the House, but was stripped out at the last minute in the Senate, which added language from another bill requiring the attorney general to “provide guidance to state agencies and others to rules regarding immigration enforcement.”

“This bill is about public safety,” Moon said Wednesday about this year’s bill. “It’s unfortunate that one year later, we do have to pull the plug on state and county participation with ICE. They have lost the public trust.”

Nine Maryland sheriff’s departments currently have a form of 287(g) agreement with ICE, under which county jails can hold a suspect for an additional two days for ICE pickup, if it is determined the suspect is not in the country legally.

The six Republicans on Judiciary, joined by Del. Frank M. Conaway Jr. (D-Baltimore City), voted against Williams’ bill Wednesday.

Del. Lauren Arikan (R-Harford) pushed back against supporters to who said 287(g) agreements are pulling local resources do go ICE’s job.

“No county that’s implemented this program has taken officers off of the street to do this at all, ever,” Arikan said. “Not how it works.”

Del. Susan McComas (R-Harford) said the bill would eliminate local control. Harford County has the second-oldest 287(g) agreement in the state, trailing only Frederick County.

“You are taking away the ability of the local leaders of those counties [and] what they deem to be necessary and important to their community and their constituents,” she said. “I think we’re going to be in litigation. This is going to be a three-ring circus, legally.”

McComas and a few other Republicans asked how much notice would be given to sheriffs and county officials if an emergency bill was approved demanding they immediately disband any agreements with ICE.

A few Democrats mentioned county officials knew about the legislature was working on a ban, with some pointing to testimony by Wicomico County Executive Julie Giordano (R) who suggested in November that her own county might want to hold off on entering into an agreement with ICE because state lawmakers might make changes to the program. Giordano announced on social media Friday that Wicomico County had signed a 287(g) agreement.

Del. N. Scott Phillips (D-Baltimore County) clarified the arrangements between local and federal authorities.

“These are MOUs [memoranda of understanding]. These are not contracts,” Phillips said. “And in each one of these MOUs, there appears to be language that applies that would allow the entities … to terminate upon request.”
